draft.shortGloss: to wear; to put on (upper-body or full-body clothing)
draft.emotion: matter-of-fact and practical, like deciding what to put on for the day
notes: Ichidan (ru-verb) transitive verb taking を. The plain form 着る means 'to put on'; the state of wearing is expressed with 着ている.
Used for upper-body and full-body clothes (shirts, coats, dresses, suits). Lower-body items (pants, skirts, shoes) take 履く (はく), hats take 被る (かぶる), and glasses take 掛ける (かける).

senses.definition: To put upper-body or full-body clothing on oneself, or (as 着ている) to have it on.

examples.text: 寒いのでコートを着る。
examples.translation: I will put on a coat because it is cold.
examples.emotion: sensible and prepared, acknowledging the change in weather

examples.text: 彼はいつも白いシャツを着ている。
examples.translation: He is always wearing a white shirt.
examples.emotion: observational and descriptive, noting a familiar habit

For accessories or items you carry (hats, glasses, watches), use 'kakeru' (掛ける) or 'kaburu' (被る).
